title: Carciofi alla Romana (Roman Braised Artichokes with Mint and Garlic)
summary: Artichokes trimmed to their tender leaves, filled with a garlicky mint and parsley mix, then braised stem up in olive oil, water and lemon until a knife slides through the base. Served with the pan juices.
equipment: saucepan just wide enough to hold the artichokes upright, with lid

ingredients.note: about 1200 g whole; about 480 g once trimmed

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to serve

steps.title: Mix the herbs
steps.text: Combine the parsley, mint, oregano, garlic, half the salt and the pepper in the small bowl.

steps.title: Trim the artichokes
steps.text: Squeeze the lemon into the cold water and drop in the halves. Pull off the dark outer leaves of each artichoke, peel the stem leaving 7-8 cm, cut off the top third and scoop out any choke. Hold them in the lemon water until all are done.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Drain the artichokes and shake them dry. Open the leaves gently and press the herb mix into the centre and between the leaves.

steps.title: Braise
steps.text: Stand the artichokes stem up in the pan. Pour over the oil, water and lemon juice and sprinkle with the remaining salt. Cover tightly and simmer over low heat for 20-30 min, until a knife meets no resistance in the base. Serve warm or at room temperature with the juices and a little more oil.

tips: Choose a pan that holds the artichokes snugly upright so they steam evenly.
If the liquid evaporates before they are tender, add a splash of hot water.
Leftover juices are excellent tossed through pasta.
storage: Refrigerate in their juices up to 3 days. Serve at room temperature or reheat gently. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
